definition: Memoization caches the result of a function under its arguments and returns the cached result on a later call with the same arguments. It turns an exponential recursion with overlapping subproblems into a much smaller number of real calls. It is the top-down form of dynamic programming.
details: It helps only when the same arguments recur. A function whose arguments are almost always new just fills the cache.
The cache key has to include every input the result depends on.

complexity.space: Proportional to the number of distinct argument combinations that are stored.

examples: Caching Fibonacci results so each n is computed once
Caching the best score for each subarray in a recursion
